---
title: "Install"
---

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/scatterem/scatterem
```

Python 3.10 or newer. Ten runtime dependencies, all from PyPI.

## About the GPU

A CUDA GPU is not optional in practice. The reconstructions are FFT- and
kernel-bound, and the NVIDIA Warp kernels that do the direct-ptychography work
need one for anything past a small test. Everything runs on CPU, just slowly
enough that you would not want to.

If the default `torch` wheel does not match your driver, install `torch` first
from the index that does, then install this package — pip will leave your
existing `torch` alone:

```bash
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
pip install git+https://github.com/scatterem/scatterem
```

`import scatterem` initialises Warp, which compiles a few kernels the first time
and prints a short banner. That is expected, and it is cached afterwards.

::: {.callout-note}
## Two side effects on import

`import scatterem` sets `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("medium")` (TF32) and
calls `warp.init()`. Both are inherited from the library the published
reconstructions ran under, so results match — but if your own code depends on
matmul precision, set it again after importing.
:::

## How much GPU memory

Peak memory is set by the *output* grid, so it grows with scan size and
upsampling rather than with detector size. Measured with
`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`:

| Reconstruction | Scan | Output | Peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amorphous carbon | 96² | 96² | ~1.2 GiB |
| Au, low dose, reduced scan | 128² | 512² | 4.4 GiB |
| Au, low dose, paper configuration | 256² | 1024² | 17.6 GiB |
| Gd₂O₃ | — | 1024² | ~19.6 GiB |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Raising `n_batches` does not reduce memory

It increases it. Measured on the Au reconstruction: `n_batches` of 15, 60 and 150
gave 17.6, 21.0 and 24.5 GiB, with bit-identical output. Halving `upsample` made
it slightly worse too.

**Shrinking the scan is the only effective lever.** Pass `scan_edge_crop` to the
named datasets, or crop your own array before constructing.
:::

## Colab

The [notebook](https://github.com/scatterem/scatterem/blob/main/docs/colab/ffstem_you2026_demo.ipynb)
runs the Au low-dose reconstruction end to end on a free T4, at a reduced scan
size that fits in 4.4 GiB. It needs a GPU runtime
(*Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU*) and nothing else — the code and the
data are both public, and the dataset downloads itself, md5-verified.

## From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/scatterem/scatterem
cd scatterem
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```
